asr.full_text: Hello my name's Simon Patmore from the BitClub Network team in the UK I just wanted to record this video to show you how to register a new member now you might already received a link from your sponsor, your upline if there is then just stick that into the address bar typically that's bitclub.bz slash user name, so in this case press that that then takes you through to the actual actual website and there's a button here called signup. Feel free to have a look around the rest of the website but click here. What then happens So put in our first name, last name, put in a email address, put in any username you want which will then check that it's valid and then put in a simple password, twice, and then you you click create account button Once you have done that, it will created your back office you'll have the ability the top right here to enroll a member so you literally click on Enroll member and you're back to the same screen the only difference is I'm now within my own account therefore I enrolled a member so it's exactly the same information and then create the account from there. Thanks very much for watching the video

visual.limitations: The sampled frames cannot establish whether any earnings occurred, what terms applied, or whether the claim was accurate.

visual.observation: A yellow instructional callout shows a referral-style URL pattern, “http://bitclub.bz/xxxxx where xxxxx = sponsor’s username,” pointing at the browser/address area.
visual.context: Visible demonstration or tutorial-style overlay; it explains how a sponsor username fits into the destination URL.
visual.potential_relevance: The destination/action is linked to a sponsor identifier, indicating a recruitment or referral relationship rather than ordinary navigation alone.
visual.limitations: The frame does not verify the website destination, the sponsor identity, or what happens after using the URL.

visual.observation: The signup page shows a sponsor field and a yellow callout saying “Make sure that this is the correct sponsor,” alongside account fields such as first name, last name, email, username, password, and password verify.
visual.context: Tutorial-like signup sequence; a note under the form appears to state users are not required to make a purchase at account creation, but the small text is only partly legible.
visual.potential_relevance: Account creation and personal-data entry are visibly conditioned on confirming a sponsor relationship.
visual.limitations: The sampled frames cannot establish whether the entered data was submitted, whether payment was later required, or whether the sponsor was correct.

visual.observation: A member page describes “BITCLUB MINING POOLS” and shows “Mining Pools Available” with “Buy Now” buttons for visible pool prices of $500, $1,000, $2,000, and $3,500.
visual.context: Member-area commercial offer context for Bitcoin mining pools; no explicit warning or denial is visible in this frame.
visual.potential_relevance: A paid purchase action is visibly tied to participation in Bitcoin mining pools and surrounding text about earning/commissions/revenue from mining-related activity.
visual.limitations: The sampled frame cannot establish purchase completion, actual mining activity, payout terms, or customer outcomes.
